thread:
maria_ops: Heads up — apiserver in ap-northeast3 is flapping during a GPU attach surge, Dedicated pool attach errors spiking. Anyone oncall? :rotating_light:

sam_sre: I'm on. seeing leader election churn in controller-manager and a bunch of 500s from apiserver. Metrics: apiserver latency jump ~200-400ms and watch queue increasing.

lee_infra: got the logs from the attach controller, lots of 'failed to dial backend: connection reset by peer'. Could be transient network or SNAT exhaustion.

maria_ops: kube-bot just alerted: `autoscale: gpu-pool-asia-dedicated` failed 3 attach attempts, fallback to hosted. @devon_plat can you check routing/MTU changes?

devon_plat: I rolled a router firmware earlier today in ap-ne3-edge; nothing obvious in rollout notes but will diff configs. Can someone paste etcd stats?

sam_sre: pasted a quick snapshot:
```
# etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.12.3.4:2379 endpoint status
10.12.3.4:2379,  3.4.15,  2.2 GiB,  1.2s
10.12.3.5:2379,  3.4.15,  2.2 GiB,  2.1s (follower)
10.12.3.6:2379,  3.4.15,  2.2 GiB,  1.9s (leader)
```
Follower latencies are elevated, leader RTT occasionally >1.5s. Not great for leader-election.

nora_research: watch cache miss rate spiked in the last 6m. Some kube-apiservers are returning 502s on list/watch and controller-manager loses lock renewal:
```
E090 11:22:15.123 controller.go:411] error getting lease: context deadline exceeded
```

lee_infra: I see a pattern: conntrack table near high watermark on the NAT boxes. `conntrack -S` shows 98% used for ap-ne3-nat-1. Likely ephemeral port exhaustion during attach fanout -> SYN retries -> large stack of half-open connections -> apiserver timeouts.

maria_ops: ack. If conntrack is saturated apiserver frontend could drop connections causing controller-manager leader flaps. What's the quick mitigation?

devon_plat: short-term: increase conntrack max on NATs, rotate NAT pool to new instances, and reduce source port reuse. Mid-term: add connection reuse on attach clients and add backpressure in the attach controller.

sam_sre: doing a quick patch to bump `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` on the two NATs now (via ansible). Also dropping a temp iptables rule to shorten TIME_WAIT for our attach paths.

kube-bot: deployment/attach-controller v2.14 rolled to canary in ap-northeast3 at 2023-09-11T11:23:45Z

maria_ops: after bumping conntrack, apiserver error rate dropped ~60% in 90s but leader election still jittery. We probably also need to tune leader-election settings for the controller-manager and scheduler while the underlying network heals.

nora_research: agree — controller-manager had lease renew failures at default 15s/10s. We can increase `--leader-elect-renew-deadline` to 20s and `--leader-elect-retry-period` to 5s as a temporary emergency config.

devon_plat: note: if etcd RTT >1s and we increase leader renew times, we need to ensure election timeout (etcd) > combined lease window. I'll open a short runbook item.

lee_infra: also found MTU discrepancy between edge router (1500) and an older tunnel (1400) created during the router rollout — fragmentation causing higher TCP stalls for snapshots and large attach payloads. Patching route to force path MTU discovery and dropping jumbo frames on the tunnel.

sam_sre: good catch. That explains intermittent RSTs in tcpdump around NVMe snapshot transfers.

maria_ops: rolling checklist for recovery:
- bump conntrack on NATs (done)
- rotate NAT pools (in progress)
- patch MTU mismatch (in progress)
- emergency leader-elect tune for controller-manager (will patch canary)
- throttle attach controller exponential backoff to avoid thundering herd (followup)

devon_plat: started NAT rotate (ap-ne3-nat-b -> ap-ne3-nat-c) and queued a config to enforce 1400 MTU on the tunnel endpoints. ETA ~8m.

kube-bot: alert resolved: apiserver error rate returned to baseline at 11:30:08Z (post-mitigation)

maria_ops: short postmortem notes: primary cause = ephemeral port / conntrack exhaustion during attach fanout combined with MTU fragmentation from a router rollout. Secondary impact = etcd follower RTT increase -> controller-manager lease renew failures -> leader election churn -> more attach retries. Cost note: Dedicated pool failed ~120 attaches and fell back to hosted for ~10m -> approx $1.9k extra egress/compute for the interim (ballpark).

nora_research: followups assigned:
- devex: add client-side attach rate limiter and better retry jitter
- infra: enforce conntrack capacity and add NAT autoscaling trigger
- net: ensure MTU validation in router rollouts
- controlplane: document emergency leader-elect tuning and add a canary that tests lease renew under degraded etcd RTTs

maria_ops: thanks everyone. I'll draft the incident blurb for all-hands and set a 1h sync to capture the followups. :white_check_mark:

sam_sre: +1, will upload logs and tcpdumps to the incident folder.

lee_infra: will keep NAT autoscale on the radar — looks like we need a small permanent bump for ap-ne3.

maria_ops: closing the thread unless new symptoms pop up.
